name: zero-postgres (sync and async PostgreSQL client)
baseline: tokio-postgres, sqlx and Diesel on PostgreSQL
verdict_reason: Its README claims 1.59x faster prepared inserts than tokio-postgres. Diesel's independent nightly suite ranks it fastest in every PostgreSQL select group (1.29x ahead of tokio-postgres and about 2x ahead of sqlx on 10,000-row selects) and within 6% of the fastest in every insert group.
tier_reason: Independent public suite (Diesel's nightly CI) with toolchain and RUSTFLAGS stated confirms the first-party README figure.
claimed_speedup: README: 10,000 prepared inserts 250.35 ms vs 398.90 ms for tokio-postgres (1.59x). Diesel suite, trivial select 10000 rows median: 1,699.58 us vs 2,190.77 us tokio-postgres, 2,419.35 us Diesel, 3,347.92 us sqlx; 100-row insert 505.93 us vs 551.50 us Diesel and 1,096.32 us sqlx (ratios derived from page data).
workload: Inserting 10,000 rows with prepared statements (README); Diesel suite trivial SELECT returning 1 to 10,000 rows and batch INSERT of 1 to 100 rows against local PostgreSQL 18.
hardware: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner (Diesel suite); not stated for the README run
os: Ubuntu (GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest image), PostgreSQL 18 on localhost
toolchain: rustc stable via rustup on the run date, RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native, cargo bench (Diesel suite)
platforms: Sync API, tokio and (experimental) compio runtimes
one_liner: New PostgreSQL client that tops Diesel's select benchmarks: 1.3x faster than tokio-postgres, about 2x sqlx on 10,000 rows.
how_it_is_fast: The name and the RefFromRow derive point to zero-copy row decoding, borrowing column data from the receive buffer instead of allocating per field. The README does not document its internals in detail.
use_it_when: Postgres row loading or bulk inserts are a measured bottleneck and you can adopt a young library
skip_it_when: You need a mature ecosystem, pooling integrations and a long track record
You need production TLS today: TLS support is marked experimental
caveats: Very new: first release December 2025, 11 GitHub stars; Diesel's suite pins version 0.8.0 while 0.9.0 is current
README benchmark gives no hardware or toolchain
Diesel-suite numbers come from a shared CI VM
tradeoffs: Young API that may change before 1.0
The repository now states BlueOak-1.0.0 while the published 0.9.0 crate says MIT
